speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a recent low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the rash is spreading?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kawasaki Disease (Note: The clinical presentation of fever >5 days, rash, and mucocutaneous symptoms is classic for Kawasaki Disease; however, the patient's age of 11 is atypical as it is most common in children under 5. Further evaluation for other causes like viral exanthems or secondary syphilis is warranted given the age and specific description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area.)
